entries.topic: Rashid Khalidi, The Hundred Years' War on Palestine (2020): summary and nodes

claims.text: Yusuf Diya al-Khalidi sent a seven-page letter on 1 March 1899 to Chief Rabbi Zadoc Kahn for Herzl; Herzl replied 19 March 1899 asking 'who would think of sending them away?'; Herzl's 1895 diary spoke of spiriting the penniless population across the border; the 1901 Jewish-Ottoman Land Company charter Herzl co-drafted provided for removal of inhabitants to other Ottoman provinces.

Khalidi frames 1917–2014 as six 'declarations of war' on the Palestinians: Balfour and the Mandate; partition and the Nakba; 1967 and Resolution 242; 1982 Lebanon; the First Intifada and Oslo; the Second Intifada and the Gaza wars.

Balfour's confidential memo (dated in the book's text as September 1919 and in its notes as 11 August 1919, printed in Documents on British Foreign Policy, 1952): in Palestine 'we do not propose even to go through the form of consulting the wishes of the present inhabitants'.
At a 1922 dinner at Balfour's home, Lloyd George, Balfour and Churchill told Weizmann that by the national home they 'always meant an eventual Jewish state' (Reinharz 1993).

Mandate articles: 2 (self-governing institutions in practice for the yishuv), 4 (Jewish Agency as public body), 6 (immigration and close settlement), 7 (nationality law); the words 'Arab' and 'Palestinian' do not appear.

Jewish share of population about 6% at end of WWI, about 18% by 1926, 17–18.5% 1926–32, over 30% by 1939; capital inflows in the 1920s averaged 41.5% above the Jewish net domestic product (Sternhell); over 60,000 immigrants in 1935; Transfer Agreement allowed German Jews to bring about $100 million (Black 1984).
Samuel nominated Hajj Amin al-Husayni as grand mufti and head of the Supreme Muslim Council after a pledge to keep order; the post of grand mufti of all Palestine and the SMC were British creations.

1936–39 revolt: six-month general strike; Peel (July 1937) proposed a Jewish state on about 17% with over 200,000 Arabs to be 'transferred'; British forces reached about 100,000; 10% of the adult male Arab population killed, wounded, imprisoned or exiled; over a hundred executions; after Andrews's assassination (Oct 1937) leaders including Mayor Husayn al-Khalidi exiled to the Seychelles for 16 months; Britain armed and trained Jewish forces during the revolt (Segev).

1939: St James's Palace conference; White Paper limited immigration and land sales and promised representative institutions in five years and self-determination in ten, contingent on all parties' agreement; Husayn al-Khalidi favoured a positive response, the mufti insisted on refusal.
King-Crane (1919) reported that military experts believed the Zionist programme could only be carried out by force of arms, requiring not less than 50,000 soldiers.
29 November 1947: Ismail al-Khalidi delivered the AHC's refusal of King Abdullah's 'protection'; Abdullah replied 'You Palestinians have refused my offer. You deserve what happens to you.'

By summer 1949 at least 720,000 of 1.3 million Palestinians were refugees; Israel held 78% of Mandate Palestine; about 160,000 Arabs remained; about 300,000 displaced before 15 May 1948 and another 400,000 after.

Jewish Brigade Group formed 1944 with Churchill's support; Arab League formed March 1945 under British aegis; Musa al-'Alami's Arab Office financed mainly by Nuri al-Sa'id's Iraq; Albert Hourani's 1946 testimony to the Anglo-American Committee; Arab National Fund raised 176,000 Palestine pounds by mid-1947 under Yusif Sayigh, against JNF collections of $3.5 million a year in the US alone in the mid-1930s.

Abdullah's secret talks with Sharett and Golda Meir (Shlaim); British–Jordanian agreement that the Arab Legion would occupy the Arab part when the Mandate ended (Mary Wilson); Shlaim: Bevin 'colluded directly with the Transjordanians and indirectly with the Jews'.

Truman, November 1945, to US diplomats: he had to answer to 'hundreds of thousands' anxious for Zionism's success (Eddy 1954); Gendzier (2015) shows the bureaucracy shifted within months after Israel's victories.

Plan Dalet cities: Tiberias 18 Apr, Haifa 23 Apr, Safad 10 May, Beisan 11 May 1948; Jaffa's 60,000 emptied in early May; Dayr Yasin 9 April: about one hundred killed, sixty-seven of them women, children and old people (W. Khalidi 1999); Abd al-Qadir al-Husayni killed at al-Qastal 8 April.
Khan Yunis (3 Nov 1956, 275 men shot) and Rafah (12 Nov 1956, 111 killed) per UNRWA director-general's special report; Qibya (Oct 1953) 69 civilians killed by Unit 101 under Sharon.
Benny Morris (Jewish Review of Books) called the book 'simply poor history'; Lisa Anderson (Foreign Affairs) called it the most cogent account from the Palestinian vantage point.
